The run_1 data shows many mechanisms fitting nearly equally well (NLL around -20), with only M9, M11, and M20 showing slightly higher (less negative) NLL. Thus, discrimination remains poor. I need to propose a new experiment that avoids extreme conditions (very low catalyst) while probing different kinetic regimes to break degeneracies.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To discriminate among mechanisms, I propose an experiment with lower substrate concentration (0.5 M) relative to catalyst (0.01 M), and include a small amount of product (0.1 M). This condition tests for saturation effects (since substrate is only 50× catalyst) and product inhibition/reversibility. Saturation behavior can differentiate simple Michaelis-Menten (M1) from mechanisms with substrate inhibition (M7), dimerization (M2, M3), or activation (M6, M8). Product presence helps distinguish reversible steps (in M1, M2, etc.) from irreversible product release, and specific product inhibition mechanisms (M12, M17). The catalyst concentration is identical to run_1, ensuring a measurable signal and avoiding numerical issues. This design explores a different region of concentration space and should provide complementary information to run_1.
</hypothesis>
